The move came after a routine Linux kernel upgrade threatened to introduce latency degradation that would measurably harm ads performance at Meta's scale. Instead of accepting the regression, Meta's engineering team built a customized scheduling policy specifically tuned for ads delivery workloads using the upstream sched_ext framework. The solution represents a shift toward using modern, extensible kernel scheduling tools rather than maintaining custom, proprietary kernel modifications. By leveraging sched_ext's BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) capabilities, Meta can now rapidly prototype and deploy scheduling policies without forking the Linux kernel or waiting for upstream changes. This approach allows the company to stay current with kernel security and performance updates while maintaining its own performance requirements. The engineering team published details of their work as part of Meta's ongoing effort to contribute to open-source infrastructure projects.

articles.hook: Meta just quietly became Python's most committed corporate supporter.
articles.headline: Meta hits decade milestone as Python Software Foundation's most reliable sponsor
articles.body: Meta has now completed 10 consecutive years of sponsoring the Python Software Foundation (PSF), the nonprofit organization that stewards Python, one of the world's most widely-used programming languages. This sustained commitment signals Meta's deep reliance on Python across its entire engineering infrastructure and reflects the company's belief in giving back to the open-source ecosystem that powers modern AI and software development. Python has become the de facto language for machine learning, data science, and AI research — areas critical to Meta's LLaMA models, recommendation systems, and broader AI strategy. By maintaining this decade-long partnership with PSF, Meta ensures the language evolves in ways that benefit not just their engineers but the thousands of companies building AI products worldwide. The sponsorship also positions Meta as a steward of developer infrastructure at a time when control over programming languages and frameworks has become strategically important in AI competition. Other major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon have similar foundation relationships, but Meta's 10-year consistency demonstrates institutional commitment beyond typical marketing partnerships.
examples: Meta engineers use Python to build and fine-tune AI models like LLaMA across distributed computing infrastructure.
Python powers Meta's recommendation algorithms that serve billions of users on Facebook and Instagram daily.
Researchers use Python to prototype new AI architectures before scaling them across Meta's data centers.
articles.build: Entrepreneurs building AI products can monetize Python expertise by offering consulting services to enterprises migrating workloads to Python-based ML stacks — typical rates are $150–300/hour for specialists. Freelancers and agencies are landing $10K–50K contracts helping companies set up Python development environments for AI projects. Some developers are creating paid courses and certifications in Python-for-AI, generating $500–$5K per student over 3–6 month programs.

articles.hook: Google just turned Search into your personal party planner.
articles.headline: Google Search AI Now Plans Your Entire Dinner Party
articles.body: Google has integrated AI capabilities into Google Search to help users plan dinner parties with features that assist in menu creation, tablescape design, and other party logistics. The announcement comes from Google AI and highlights how search engines are evolving beyond information retrieval into actionable planning tools. These AI features leverage Google's existing language and creative models to generate personalized suggestions based on user preferences, dietary restrictions, guest count, and aesthetic goals. Rather than manually browsing multiple websites for recipes, decoration ideas, and timeline advice, users can now ask Google Search directly and receive curated recommendations. The integration demonstrates how AI is moving into everyday life tasks that previously required hours of research across multiple sources. Google doesn't specify which exact model powers these features, but they likely leverage Gemini technology. The real-world impact is significant for content creators, event planners, and entrepreneurs who can use these AI-assisted features to streamline client consultations, offer faster turnaround times on party proposals, and potentially upsell premium design services built on top of these AI suggestions.
examples: Ask Google Search for a three-course menu for 8 people with one vegan guest and Mediterranean theme.
Get tablescape design ideas matching your menu, color scheme, and budget constraints instantly.
Generate a timeline from shopping list to plating for your dinner party with specific cooking steps.
articles.build: Event planners are charging $500-$2,000 for full dinner party planning services and now offering 'AI-assisted rapid planning' at $200-$400 to price-conscious clients who want faster turnaround. Etsy sellers and Pinterest creators are building premium 'dinner party AI planning templates' selling for $15-$50 each, combining Google Search outputs with branded design elements. Caterers are using this to pitch 'done-for-you menu creation' add-ons to clients for $100-$300 per event.
